title: Rook endings: four habits and where they fail
outcomes: Puts the rook behind a passed pawn and predicts how the result changes when the rook stands in front of it
Predicts win or draw with the rook on the seventh rank, and names a position where the seventh rank is not enough
Finds the defender's far check instead of a close one, and spots a position with no passed pawn, where the rook-behind habit does not apply

steps.text:
Four rook-ending habits.
**Behind:** put the rook behind a passed pawn.
**Cut off:** keep the enemy king away along a file or rank.
**Seventh:** a rook on the seventh rank can shut the enemy king on the back rank.
**Distance:** the defender's rook checks from far away.
Each is a *rule of thumb* with exceptions. A **tablebase** (exact results for few pieces) checks every position.

steps.caption: White to move wins. The rook stands on e4, behind the passed pawn on e5. One line is shown.

line.say: The pawn advances. The rook on e4 defends it from behind along the open file.
Black's rook runs to the far end of the board.
The pawn reaches e7. The rook still defends it from behind, across more squares.
Black's rook takes the square in front of the pawn.
White's king steps up the board towards the pawn.

claims.statement: White wins from the start position.
The pawn on e5 is passed.
After e6 the rook defends the pawn.
After e7 the rook still defends the pawn.

steps.text: **Why behind?** From behind, the rook keeps the whole file ahead of the pawn in view after every push. In front of the pawn it loses a square with each push. This is a *rule of thumb*: sometimes the passive rook is right, and you will meet that exception below. First test the habit: predict each position, then check.

steps.title: Behind or in front?
steps.prompt: In the first position White's rook is behind its passed pawn. Predict the other two, then check.

steps.text:
**Seventh rank:** a rook there attacks the whole rank if it is open, keeping the enemy king on the back rank. It is strongest with an advanced passed pawn, but no guarantee.
**Distance:** the defender's rook checks from far away, where the king cannot attack it. A check right next to the king can simply lose the rook.
Both are *rules of thumb*. Predict, then check.

steps.title: The rook on the seventh rank
steps.prompt: In the first position White's rook is on the seventh rank and Black's king is shut in on a8. Predict the other two, then check.
Think back to the three silent positions. Which of the four habits did you reach for first in each, and in which one did an exception catch you?
